secure_admin.title: Secure the admin account
secure_admin.what: Add a second sign-in check, either an authenticator app code (two-factor) or a passkey (sign in with your fingerprint, face or device PIN), to the account that controls every deployment.
secure_admin.why: A stolen password alone should never be enough to reach your servers.

sign_in_recovery.title: Set up a way back in
sign_in_recovery.what: Connect email, or approve new sign-ins from a device you already trust, so you can get back in if you lose your password.
sign_in_recovery.why: If you lose your password or passkey, this is how you get back to your servers.

security_review.title: Review your security defaults
security_review.what: Look over the protections that ship turned on, such as webhook replay protection and audit of sensitive reads, and change any that do not fit your setup.
security_review.why: These defaults are safe for most installs. Reviewing them once means no protection is off by accident.

public_address.title: Set the dashboard address and turn on HTTPS
public_address.what: Pick the web address you open this dashboard on. The free option is the https address built from this server's IP, with a real certificate and no DNS setup.
public_address.why: Once HTTPS is on, signing in over plain HTTP stops working, so this is best done early.

git_provider.title: Connect a git source or deploy an image
git_provider.what: Link GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket or Gitea so a push deploys your app. If you deploy a ready-made container image instead, skip this.
git_provider.why: Linked repositories give you automatic deploys and a deploy history tied to commits.

first_app.title: Deploy your first app
first_app.what: Create an app from a repository, a container image or a template. The platform builds it, starts it and gives it an https address.
first_app.why: It proves the build, deploy and rollback loop works on this server.

app_domain.title: Put the app on your domain
app_domain.what: Attach your own hostname to the app and point its DNS record (the entry at your domain registrar) at this server.
app_domain.why: Real users reach the app by name, not by an IP address and port.

dns.title: Connect a DNS provider or proxy
dns.what: Let the platform edit DNS records for you through Cloudflare or Route 53, or run it behind a reverse proxy you already have.
dns.why: Records and certificates stop being manual copy and paste.

tls.title: Check the app's HTTPS certificate
tls.what: Confirm every domain serves a certificate browsers trust and that it renews on its own (TLS is the encryption behind https).
tls.why: Browsers warn on invalid certificates, and a silent renewal failure takes the app down.

backup_target.title: Add a backup target
backup_target.what: Send backups to storage that is not on this server, any S3-compatible service such as AWS S3, Backblaze B2 or Cloudflare R2.
backup_target.why: A backup on the same disk does not survive the disk.

first_backup.title: Take the first backup
first_backup.what: Save a copy of the platform's own database, which holds every app definition, so it can be recovered.
first_backup.why: Losing that database means losing every app definition.

verified_restore.title: Verify a restore
verified_restore.what: Run a verification on a backup to prove it can actually be restored.
verified_restore.why: An untested backup is a hope, not a backup.

notifications.title: Add a notification channel and alert rule
notifications.what: Send alerts to email, Slack, Discord, Telegram or a webhook, then create an alert rule that uses it.
notifications.why: You hear about a crashloop or an expiring certificate before your users do.

teammate.title: Invite a teammate
teammate.what: Give a second person access so the platform does not depend on one login.
teammate.why: Someone else can act when you are away. Skip it for a solo setup.

upgrades.title: Choose an upgrade policy
upgrades.what: Decide how the platform updates itself: automatically in a window, or only when you say so.
upgrades.why: Security fixes reach you without a surprise restart in the middle of the day.
